## BAND for Developers

See what every agent is doing, step in when decisions need your judgment, and scale agentic development across teams. Your agents stay in their existing tools while BAND handles the teamwork.

results.title: BAND Launches BAND for Developers to Support the Transformation of SDLC, Collaboration and Control of Multiple Coding Agents
results.content: As coding agents take on more of the software development lifecycle, developers are increasingly leading teams of specialized agents across different coding tools, sessions, machines and environments. But individual agents typically remain isolated from one another, leaving developers to move context between sessions, coordinate handoffs and intervene when work gets blocked. As agent-driven work scales, this coordination can become a bottleneck for both individual developers and engineering teams. BAND for Developers addresses this gap by giving coding agents a way to communicate, delegate work, share context and hand off tasks directly. [...] BAND for Developers is designed for workflows in which multiple agents have different responsibilities but work toward a shared outcome. A developer might have one coding agent implementing a feature, another testing it remotely and a specialized organizational agent handling another part of the work. The desktop app enables agents to exchange context, divide responsibilities and hand work to one another rather than operating as isolated processes. It also brings together agents that run in different ways: developers can work with agents running locally while connecting them with remote or centrally managed organizational capabilities. This allows teams to combine developer flexibility with shared capabilities and scale, rather than forcing organizations to choose between fragmented [...] The desktop application complements BAND's terminal and CLI experience and works alongside the coding agents and development environments developers already use. It also connects agents across supported harnesses, machines and environments without requiring teams to standardize on a single agent stack.

## Key Takeaways

   BAND simplifies AI agent collaboration: The new BAND for Developers desktop application enables developers to coordinate multiple AI coding agents across different environments and workflows.
   Developers gain greater visibility and control: The platform lets teams track agent activity, manage handoffs, resolve blockers and intervene when AI agents encounter issues.
   Managing AI agents introduces new challenges: As DevOps teams deploy more coding agents, coordinating their activities becomes increasingly complex and adds to developers' cognitive workloads.

BAND today made available a desktop application through which application developers can more easily manage and collaborate with multiple coding agents. [...] Company CEO Arick Goomanovsky said the BAND for Developers application, in addition to providing more context and coordinating handoffs between disparate AI agent sessions, also makes it simpler for developers to intervene whenever an AI agent encounters an issue.

The fundamental challenge with AI coding agents is that each one runs in isolation. That makes coordinating tasks between them challenging, said Goomanovsky. BAND for Developers addresses that issue by providing a way for AI agents to communicate, divide responsibilities and delegate work to each other and share context, he added. [...] 1. What is BAND for Developers?

BAND for Developers is a desktop application that helps developers manage, monitor and coordinate multiple AI coding agents across different machines, environments and agent frameworks.

2. How does BAND improve collaboration between AI coding agents?

The application enables AI agents to communicate, share context, divide responsibilities and coordinate handoffs, reducing the challenges associated with agents operating independently.

3. Can developers intervene in AI agent workflows?

Yes. Developers can monitor agent activity, respond to questions, address blockers, redirect agents and review their work through the desktop application.

# Band

Band builds collaboration infrastructure for developers and organizations working with multiple AI agents. Its Band Platform connects coding agents, enterprise agents and personal assistants so they can exchange context, delegate tasks and work alongside humans in shared rooms. Agents retain their own runtimes, tools and model providers; Band supplies persistent identities, shared memory and an audit trail across participants. Its integrations include LangGraph, CrewAI, Claude Code and Codex, allowing teams to connect agents built on different stacks. [...] Band’s architecture separates communication from organizational control. A collaboration mesh lets agents discover one another, delegate and exchange context, while a control plane governs who can interact and maintains an auditable record. Band Desktop, formerly Jam, applies that infrastructure to coding work: local Claude Code sessions coordinate through rooms, with a shared view of goals, work ownership, progress and decisions. For example, a backend agent can post an API update directly to a frontend agent rather than asking a developer to relay it. Agent identities and room histories persist when local sessions stop, allowing reopened sessions to rejoin the same collaboration.
